open_questions.q: Is the H2730R plasmid actually intact-identical to p18-43_01 (212,326 bp), or does the 100.000% identity over 14,979 bp of contig 22 only reflect a shared blaNDM-1-region cassette while the rest of the plasmid backbone has diverged?
open_questions.basis: The central pathogenomic claim was reproduced at 100.000% identity across the entire 14,979 bp of contig NZ_VWTQ01000022.1 against CP023554.1 positions 61316-76294, and contigs 27, 31, 41 also align at >=99% identity. But short-read Illumina/SKESA assemblies cannot resolve a 212 kbp multireplicon plasmid as a single closed circle. Whether H2730R carries an intact copy of p18-43_01 vs a mosaic plasmid that only shares the NDM-1 island remains unresolved by both the paper and this replication.
next_steps: Long-read resequence H2730R with Oxford Nanopore (R10.4.1) + PacBio HiFi to obtain a closed plasmid
Hybrid assemble with Unicycler / Trycycler; report plasmid completeness + circularity flag
Do full pairwise plasmid alignment (MUMmer nucmer, minimap2 asm5) vs CP023554.1 and generate a Mauve/synteny plot
Report percent-identity, coverage, and structural rearrangements across the full 212 kbp

open_questions.q: Does the acquired-resistance-gene count discrepancy (paper=25 vs this run=17 distinct loci) reflect true additional genes in the paper's ResFinder+ARG-ANNOT+CARD union, or is it pure subfamily double-counting?
open_questions.basis: This replication used a single PGAP+regex pass and detected 17 distinct acquired R-loci covering every drug class the paper reports. The paper's number is a tool-union across three databases with known subfamily-overlap inflation. Without the paper's per-database output tables, it is not possible to reconstruct which specific 8 additional entries the union produced or whether any are genuine hits missed by PGAP annotation.
next_steps: Rerun ResFinder 4.x, CARD RGI (strict + loose), and AMRFinderPlus against GCF_015208815.1
Deduplicate by locus coordinates rather than by tool-reported name
Compare against the deposited resistome file if any exists in BV-BRC or the paper's SI
Report both raw union count and deduplicated distinct-locus count so the two conventions are separable

open_questions.q: Does H2730R actually carry the GyrA S83I substitution associated with fluoroquinolone resistance, or is the quinolone resistance phenotype entirely explained by PMQR (qnrB1, aac(6')-Ib-cr) plus efflux?
open_questions.basis: Claim C17 (GyrA S83I) is marked PARTIAL in this replication because the gyrA CDS is present on contig 6 but the specific serine-83-to-isoleucine substitution was not extracted. C18 (qnrB1 + aac(6')-Ib-cr) is confirmed. The clinical significance of the quinolone-resistance verdict depends on whether the QRDR (quinolone resistance-determining region) mutation is present in addition to the plasmid-mediated determinants.
next_steps: Extract gyrA protein sequence from the assembly (translate CDS on contig 6)
Align vs a wild-type E. coli K-12 GyrA reference (UniProt P0AES4) with clustalo or mafft
Report the amino acid at position 83 (and 87 for parC-adjacent QRDR sites)
Also verify parC S80I and other canonical QRDR positions

open_questions.q: Is Citrobacter freundii ST498 an emerging South African clone with additional public isolates, or is H2730R a singleton at the time of this replication?
open_questions.basis: The paper describes ST498 as 'novel' but does not comment on subsequent PubMLST accumulation. This replication confirmed ST498 exists as a canonical PubMLST record and that H2730R matches it, but did not enumerate how many other isolates have since been submitted with the same ST or how many are also NDM-1+ / from South Africa / from the same hospital / from the same p18-43_01 lineage.
next_steps: Query PubMLST C. freundii scheme 1 for all ST498 records; export country / year / source metadata
Cross-reference NCBI Pathogen Detection cluster (PDG) for isolates linked to GCF_015208815.1
Look for other South African NDM-1+ C. freundii submissions (2020-present) and cluster by SNP distance
Report whether ST498 is now recognized as an emerging XDR clone or remains a singleton

open_questions.q: Are the four plasmid replicons (Inc A/C2, Inc FIB(pB171), Inc FII(Yp), Inc Q1) that the paper reports via PlasmidFinder actually all present in the assembly, and on which contigs do they sit?
open_questions.basis: Claim C13 was not re-run in this replication (PlasmidFinder is a web-only tool the paper used). PGAP annotation on contig 19 shows a RepA IncFII-family replicon, giving partial support for IncFII(Yp), but the full four-replicon typing was not reproduced. Because H2730R is XDR and multi-plasmid strains are common in NDM-1 Enterobacterales, resolving the replicon set is important for both epidemiology (which plasmid families are circulating) and mechanism (which plasmids carry which resistance genes).
next_steps: Run PlasmidFinder 2.x locally against GCF_015208815.1_ASM1520881v1_genomic.fna
Map each replicon hit to its host contig and cross-reference with the resistance-gene contigs (22, 27, 31, 40, 41, 53)
Build a per-plasmid resistance-load table (which replicon co-locates with which R gene)
Compare with MOB-suite for plasmid clustering and mobility prediction
